A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MOS research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including v2's new Appendices B and C.

before.justification: v1 reports original MOS evaluations, sharing experiments, and component ablations in Tables 1–3, alongside explicitly attributed baseline results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds LLaMA3.2-3B experiments, hyperparameter sensitivity results, statistical analyses, and training-time measurements.

M1.justification: Global sharing and the four differentiation strategies remain unchanged. Renaming Index to Route and explaining unified implementation and possible precomputation clarify the existing fixed-index procedure without establishing an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use SuperNI, Flan V2 and its CoT mixture, and CodeAlpaca for training, with MMLU, BBH, GSM8K, TyDi QA, and HumanEval evaluation. The additional experiments retain these tasks; LLaMA3.2-3B extends model configurations rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding original comparisons retain LoRA, VeRA, Tied LoRA, PRoLoRA, vanilla models, and sharing controls. The appended experiments reuse existing comparison methods and introduce no new baseline method.

E3.justification: v2 adds LLaMA3.2-3B experiments with one epoch of finetuning alongside the retained 10,000-step LLaMA2 experiments. It also introduces a BBH grid over private ranks and shard counts. Existing benchmark metrics, preprocessing, and prompting settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations, v2 repeats sharing/differentiation controls on LLaMA3.2-3B, analyzes seed stability, and adds a private-rank-by-shard sensitivity study in Appendix B. Appendix C adds measured training overhead, substantially broadening the robustness and efficiency analyses.

E5.justification: v1 reports averages from seeds 0 and 1 without uncertainty estimates. v2 retains that disclosure and adds four-seed experiments using seeds 0–3, standard deviations in Table 5, and significance tests for two LLaMA2-7B parameter budgets in Table 7. The significance-test procedure is not specified.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their numerical results. New Tables 4–8 add model results, sensitivity scores, p-values, and timings. For example, the new LLaMA3.2-3B comparison reports averages of 45.38 for MOS with 12.16M parameters and 45.41 for LoRA with 97.26M parameters; Table 8 reports 2.80% additional aggregate training time.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds a limited combinatorial derivation connecting differentiation to counts of possible matrix combinations: one under pure sharing, binomial selection counts, squared counts after dissociation, and larger counts after sharding. v1 provides only the qualitative diversity argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: differentiation enables effective sharing, MOS combines four strategies, and approximately eightfold parameter savings are achievable. The additional experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix C acknowledges greater GPU consumption at equal trainable-parameter budgets and possible routing latency, suggesting precomputation as mitigation. Appendix B adds interpretations of seed stability and the relationship between private rank and shard count.

D1.justification: v2 announces an official code location, identifies higher-rank selections for individual Table 2 results, and explains treating rank as a hyperparameter. It also documents the added model's training budget, sensitivity-grid settings, and measured training times.

R1.justification: Section 5 removes the brief DyLoRA comparison and adds citations to already-listed LoRA enhancement papers. DyLoRA remains cited in Section 3.3 and the bibliography; the reference list and broader research positioning are otherwise unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section order are retained. v2 adds a Unity paragraph, appendix cross-references, Appendices B and C, and acknowledgements, with limited terminology edits and expanded affiliation text.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands quantitative presentation with appendix tables displaying additional model comparisons, standard deviations, a hyperparameter grid, significance tests, and training costs. Table 2 gains rank annotations and explanatory notes, Table 3 relocates, and author/header formatting changes. Figures 1–2 remain substantively unchanged.

improvement.justification: Additional model validation, uncertainty reporting, clearer rank/code information, and explicit computational limitations improve evidential support and transparency. These gains are tempered by unspecified significance-test procedures and an overstatement in Appendix B.3: Table 6's private-rank-7 maximum is 39.6%, contradicting the claim that every private rank permits at least 39.8%. Overall, the additions provide a limited net improvement.
